clue.text: Spun sacks weaver finally developed

indicators.note: sacks means dismisses, so a letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: spun means revolved, turned round

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word weaver

explanation.surface: A weaver spinning yarn into sacks gradually develops the craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacks' looks like a noun of the weaving scene, but it is the verb: REVOLVED sacks R, the last letter of 'weaver'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evolved has grown or changed gradually, which is what developed means.

clue.text: Case of ale, ultimately 10's more than enough

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word ale

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
ample means more than enough, plentiful

explanation.surface: A crate of beer, ten bottles being plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a box of ale, but it means an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an instance, as is a specimen illustrating a rule.

clue.text: Painting geriatric Pole's given to the Queen

parts.note: geriatric means old
a mast is a tall pole
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An elderly Polish man presents a painting to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with its capital looks like a Polish person, but it is a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas by a great European artist before about 1800 is called by this name.

clue.text: Place by road that's lacking its roof

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top letter, here taken away

parts.note: an avenue is a broad road

explanation.surface: A building by the road with no roof on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is a location where an event takes place.

clue.text: Insult syllabus in verbal communication

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for insulting them
a course of study follows a syllabus

explanation.surface: A student insults the syllabus while speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is spoken or written communication, especially talk and debate.

clue.text: Fiery affair enthralling a male

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair

explanation.surface: A passionate affair captivates a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaming describes something on fire or burning hotly, a synonym of fiery.

clue.text: Female expert daughter confronted

parts.note: an ace is an expert
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A skilled woman's daughter stood up to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem is to confront it head on.

clue.text: Rule trade out with one known to cheat

indicators.note: out means wrong or off, so these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Banning a trade comes along with a known swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer is unfaithful to a spouse, cheating on them.

clue.text: One kiss and I love new free- wheeling king

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A carefree king trades a kiss and a declaration of love.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Ixion, a king of Thessaly, was bound by Zeus to a fiery wheel forever, hence the wheeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ixion was a mythical king punished on a spinning wheel, so a wheeling king.

clue.text: On The Town possibly is dated

definitions.meaning: a night on the town is an evening spent away from home socialising
something old-fashioned is no longer in style

explanation.walkthrough: 'On The Town' looks like the musical's title, but means a night spent out.
explanation.definitionFit: Having gone out is being out on the town, and a fashion that has gone out is dated.

clue.text: Extra in commercial showing around Germany

indicators.note: around means the first pieces go round the next one

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a film or show that is on is showing
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A bonus feature turns up in an advert screened across Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is a supplementary item, something extra bolted onto the main thing.

clue.text: Uncle is so active in retirement

indicators.note: active means busy and moving about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncle stays busy even after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like stopping work, but here it means withdrawing from company.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement can mean withdrawal into privacy, a state of being cut off from others.

clue.text: A crate-full of dope all ruined, article admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other
ruined means wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A whole crate of drugs is spoiled, as a smuggler confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crate' is old slang for an aircraft, so a crate-full is a full load for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is informal for an old aeroplane, so its full cargo is an aircraft's load.

clue.text: Dance hit by Pan released at last

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

indicators.note: released at last means the final letter is let go

parts.note: Pan is a Greek god

explanation.surface: A dancer is struck by Peter Pan, who has finally been let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan is the Greek god of the wild, not Peter Pan; GOD loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Consumer worry that's flipping concerning

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A shopper frets about something that is flipping worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats food consumes it, so a diner is a consumer.

clue.text: Suffering cats and dogs and other pets in war

indicators.note: other means different, so these letters take another form

explanation.surface: Cats, dogs and other pets suffer during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' look like pets, but suffering cats and dogs means being rained on heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Raining cats and dogs is an idiom for a downpour, so a place lashed by it is storm-battered.

clue.text: Flapper in recumbent convalescence, Spooner said

indicators.note: Spooner's slips swapped the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: recumbent means lying down, as in bed
rest is what convalescence requires

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper is laid up in bed recovering, says the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a jazz-age young woman, but it is a bird that flaps. Spooner turns BED REST round.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapper is crossword slang for a bird, and the robin is the familiar bird with a red front.

clue.text: Finding cod's very bad around lunchtime?

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round another piece
bad means rotten, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is I

explanation.surface: Discovering the cod has gone off around lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, so a finding.

clue.text: Cocktail and pale pint I ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: At the bar I ordered a cocktail and a pint of pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An appletini is a vodka-and-apple martini-style cocktail.

clue.text: Resilience shown by princess caught in animal tether

indicators.note: caught in means held inside another piece

parts.note: a harness straps up a horse or dog
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A princess shows toughness when tangled in a horse's straps.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Di is Diana, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiness is toughness and the ability to withstand hardship, close kin to resilience.

clue.text: Part of football match with appeal for idiot

parts.note: a football match is played in two halves
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: During a football half someone makes a foolish appeal to the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Quick attack secures front for paras

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly within

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: front for picks the opening letter of paras

explanation.surface: A fast assault by paratroopers seizes the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or swift, a direct synonym of quick.

clue.text: Only gad about from dawn to dusk

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: The only thing to do is wander around all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting the whole day, from sunrise to sunset, is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Picks up presents German changed for large

indicators.note: changed for means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: gifts are presents
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Someone collects presents, swapping a German one for a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: G (German) in GIFTS is changed for L (large).
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise or pick it up.

clue.text: Look in bog for criminal from Texas

indicators.note: in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: a fen is a marshy bog
lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Search the marsh for a Texan outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The Texas tag fits the American legal term felony for a serious crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone convicted of a serious crime, a term of US law.

clue.text: Another easy bit of anti-infection precautions

indicators.note: another means a different version, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: One more simple piece of advice about preventing infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Biosafety covers the safeguards against spreading dangerous pathogens in labs and hospitals.

clue.text: Pompous type of bishop with affected walk?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a limp is a walk affected by injury

explanation.surface: A self-important bishop with an affected gait.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a British cartoon of a pompous, reactionary old officer.
explanation.definitionFit: From the cartoon Colonel Blimp, the word names a pompous, reactionary person.

clue.text: School head must leave, one near Bow?

indicators.note: head must leave means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school head must quit, one living near Bow in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of east London, but here it is the archer's weapon. HARROW is an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is fitted to a bow when shooting, so sits beside one.

clue.text: Animal owner with vile bats

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pet's keeper owns some nasty bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals, but it is slang for mad, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a stocky carnivorous mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Beastly type that could charge you money

definitions.meaning: an animal known for charging with its horn

explanation.surface: An animal that might bill you for its services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' teases a fee, but here the beast stampedes; the money sense is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal charges at threats, and in dated British slang the word also means money.

clue.text: Item of gear in the turret of a Panzer?

definitions.text: Item of gear in the turret of a Panzer?

parts.words: Item of gear in the turret of a Panzer?
parts.note: a garment named as if it were the upper part of an armoured war vehicle

explanation.surface: A piece of equipment found in a German tank's turret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' suggests military kit, but means clothing: a sleeveless knitted jumper whose name reads as the turret of a Panzer, a German tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless knitted pullover is an item of clothing, and gear is slang for clothes.

clue.text: Canopy, after year, showing sign of fatigue?

indicators.note: after means the canopy word comes second, following the year letter

parts.note: an awning is a canopy over a shopfront

explanation.surface: A shop canopy, a year on, looks tired and worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the canopy after the year letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening the mouth wide in a gape is the classic sign of tiredness.
